newsitem.title: POLAND: ING Barings says Warsaw bourse slowdown likely.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings says Warsaw bourse slowdown likely.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse may be approaching an overbought position leading to a more gradual appreciation or a correction, ING Barings said in its Emerging Europe Stratgegy report for February 1997.

"While we are long-term positive on the market and feel that both prospects for earnings and the current valuation continue to look attractive, now may well be a good time to take some profit," the report said.
ING Barings retained its view that 1997 earnings would rebound strongly but revised down its market nominal earnings growth to 21 percent from almost 24 percent in December.
It said industrial earnings would grow by 24.5 percent.

"While this translates into around five-percent growth after inflation, with the zloty expected to remain flat in real terms...in hard currency terms measured against the zloty's basket this translates into almost 12-percent growth in EPS for the market and close to 16 percent for industrials," it said.
ING Barings said it remained overweight in the foods, paint and computer sectors and raised its view on glass maker Irena to overweight.
It said it remained underweight in banking stocks but stayed overweight in construction after good 1996 earnings results and a satisfactory outlook for 1997's first quarter.
ING Barings said equity performance later this year would likely be constrained by sizeable IPOs and secondary offerings, despite listed firms' healthy earnings prospects.

"Risk-averse investors unbridled by restrictions on the choice of asset class should favour fixed income over equities while, for an equity-specific investor looking to stabilise return characteristics within an equity portfolio, a measure of local fixed income would certainly help," the report said.
